title: Prakrama 2, Sarga 15. Description of the Gopis' Mood — Bhakti-yoga
html:
The Lord speaks of His vision of Varaha and Halayudha and asks for His flute; in Chandrashekhara's house a play is staged: the Lord in women's dress, Srivasa as Narada, Gadadhara as a gopi; Narada speaks of the greatness of devotion

Verse 1

उवाच कृष्णः कलनादरम्यं
वचोऽमृतं श्लाघ्यसगद्गदस्वरम्।
वराहदेवो भगवान्ददौ मा-
मालिङ्गनं यज्ञवपुर्महीधरः॥१॥

uvāca kṛṣṇaḥ kalanādaramyaṁ
vaco'mṛtaṁ ślāghyasagadgadasvaram|
varāhadevo bhagavāndadau mā-
māliṅganaṁ yajñavapurmahīdharaḥ||1||

uvacha — spoke; krishnah — Krishna (Gaura); kala-nada-ramyam — charming with its soft tone; vachah — words; amritam — nectarean; shlaghya-sa-gadgada-svaram — in a lovely, faltering voice; varaha-devah — Lord Varaha; bhagavan — Bhagavan; dadau — gave; mam — me; alinganam — an embrace; yajna-vapuh — whose body is sacrifice; mahidharah — the Upholder of the earth.

1Krishna spoke nectarean words, charming in their soft tone, in a lovely, faltering voice: "Lord Varaha, whose body is sacrifice, the Upholder of the earth, has embraced Me1.

Verse 2

हलायुधो मे हृदि सन्निविष्टः
स वेणुपाणिर्नयनाञ्जनोऽभूत्।
इतीरितं तस्य निशम्य विप्रा
हृष्टा ननन्दुर्ननृतुर्महान्तः॥२॥

halāyudho me hṛdi sanniviṣṭaḥ
sa veṇupāṇirnayanāñjano'bhūt|
itīritaṁ tasya niśamya viprā
hṛṣṭā nanandurnanṛturmahāntaḥ||2||

halayudhah — Halayudha; me — my; hridi — in the heart; sannivishtah — has entered; sah — He; venu-panih — flute in hand; nayana-anjanah — a salve for the eyes; abhut — became; iti — thus; iritam — what was said; tasya — His; nishamya — hearing; viprah — the brahmanas; hrishtah — thrilled; nananduh — rejoiced; nanrituh — danced; mahantah — the great.

2Halayudha has entered My heart — and has become the One with the flute in His hand, a salve for the eyes2." Hearing these words of His, the great brahmanas rejoiced in delight and danced.

Verse 3

श्रीवासमाह प्रहसन्स कृष्णो
वेणुं प्रयच्छाद्य मदीयमुत्तमम्।
तदावदत्सोऽपि तवालये विभो
भीष्मात्मजायाः परिरक्षितोऽस्ति सः॥३॥

śrīvāsamāha prahasansa kṛṣṇo
veṇuṁ prayacchādya madīyamuttamam|
tadāvadatso'pi tavālaye vibho
bhīṣmātmajāyāḥ parirakṣito'sti saḥ||3||

shrivasam — to Srivasa; aha — said; prahasan — laughing; sah — He; krishnah — Krishna; venum — the flute; prayachchha — give; adya — now; madiyam — My; uttamam — excellent; tada — then; avadat — said; sah — he; api — also; tava — Your; alaye — in the house; vibho — O Lord; bhishma-atmajayah — by Bhishmaka's daughter; parirakshitah — guarded; asti — is; sah — it.

3Laughing, Krishna said to Srivasa: "Give Me My excellent flute now!" He replied: "Lord, it is in Your house, kept by the daughter of Bhishmaka3.

Verse 4

वेणुस्तदस्मिन्समये न लभ्यते
रात्रौ कवाटापिहिते गृहान्तरे।
एवं निशम्य प्रहसन्निशां तां
भक्तैः समं लोकगुरुर्निनाय॥४॥

veṇustadasminsamaye na labhyate
rātrau kavāṭāpihite gṛhāntare|
evaṁ niśamya prahasanniśāṁ tāṁ
bhaktaiḥ samaṁ lokagururnināya||4||

venuh — the flute; tat — so; asmin samaye — at this time; na labhyate — cannot be had; ratrau — at night; kavata-apihite — with the door shut; griha-antare — in the inner rooms; evam — thus; nishamya — hearing; prahasan — laughing; nisham — night; tam — that; bhaktaih — with the devotees; samam — together; loka-guruh — the Teacher of the world; ninaya — spent.

4The flute cannot be had at this hour: it is night, and the door of the inner rooms is shut." Hearing this, the Teacher of the world laughed, and spent that night with the devotees.

Verse 5

प्रातर्ययुस्ते मुदिता द्विजेशा
नत्वा हरिं स्वःसरिदम्बुमध्ये।
स्नात्वा सुखेनैव हरिं समर्च्य
भुक्त्वा प्रसादं परमां मुदं ययुः॥५॥

prātaryayuste muditā dvijeśā
natvā hariṁ svaḥsaridambumadhye|
snātvā sukhenaiva hariṁ samarcya
bhuktvā prasādaṁ paramāṁ mudaṁ yayuḥ||5||

pratah — in the morning; yayuh — went; te — those; muditah — joyful; dvija-ishah — lords of the twice-born; natva — bowing to; harim — Hari; svah-sarit-ambu-madhye — into the waters of the heavenly river; snatva — having bathed; sukhena eva — happily; harim — Hari; samarchya — having worshipped; bhuktva — having eaten; prasadam — prasada; paramam — supreme; mudam — joy; yayuh — attained.

5In the morning the joyful lords of the twice-born bowed to Hari and went to the waters of the heavenly river; having bathed, they gladly worshipped Hari, partook of prasada and were filled with supreme joy.

Verse 6

एवं महाक्रीडनकं मुरारेः
श्रुत्वा विमुच्येत भवार्णवान्नरः।
पठेल्लभेत्तत्पदपङ्कजे रतिं
द्रुतं महारोगगणाद्विमुच्यते॥६॥

evaṁ mahākrīḍanakaṁ murāreḥ
śrutvā vimucyeta bhavārṇavānnaraḥ|
paṭhellabhettatpadapaṅkaje ratiṁ
drutaṁ mahārogagaṇādvimucyate||6||

evam — thus; maha-kridanakam — the great play; murareh — of Murari (Krishna); shrutva — hearing; vimuchyeta — will be freed; bhava-arnavat — from the ocean of existence; narah — a person; pathet — should recite; labhet — will gain; tat-pada-pankaje — for His lotus feet; ratim — love; drutam — quickly; maha-roga-ganat — from hosts of grave diseases; vimuchyate — is freed.

6Whoever hears of this great play of Murari4 will be freed from the ocean of existence; whoever recites it will gain love for His lotus feet and will quickly be freed from hosts of grave diseases.

Verse 7

यस्य पादकमले कमलायाः
प्रीतिसागरवरो मुहुर्बभौ।
तस्य कृष्णपदपङ्कजाश्रये
गोपयौवतवशेऽभवन्मनः॥७॥

yasya pādakamale kamalāyāḥ
prītisāgaravaro muhurbabhau|
tasya kṛṣṇapadapaṅkajāśraye
gopayauvatavaśe'bhavanmanaḥ||7||

yasya — at whose; pada-kamale — lotus feet; kamalayah — of Kamala; priti-sagara-varah — a splendid ocean of love; muhuh — ever; babhau — shone; tasya — His; krishna-pada-pankaja-ashraye — in taking shelter of Krishna's lotus feet; gopa-yauvata-vashe — under the sway (of the mood) of the young cowherd women; abhavat — came; manah — mind.

7At His lotus feet the splendid ocean of Kamala's love ever shone; and now His mind, seeking shelter at the lotus feet of Krishna, came under the sway of the mood of the young cowherd women.

Verse 8

एकदा समभिधाय सुवेशं
योषितां स्मितसुधामुखचन्द्रः।
चन्द्रशेखरगृहाङ्गने विभु-
र्नर्तनं निजजनैः स चकार॥८॥

ekadā samabhidhāya suveśaṁ
yoṣitāṁ smitasudhāmukhacandraḥ|
candraśekharagṛhāṅgane vibhu-
rnartanaṁ nijajanaiḥ sa cakāra||8||

ekada — once; samabhidhaya — putting on; su-vesham — the beautiful attire; yoshitam — of women; smita-sudha-mukha-chandrah — His moon-face shedding the nectar of smiles; chandrashekhara-griha-angane — in the courtyard of Chandrashekhara's house; vibhuh — the Lord; nartanam — a dance; nija-janaih — with His own; sah — He; chakara — performed.

8Once the Lord, whose moon-face sheds the nectar of smiles, put on the beautiful attire of a woman and held a dance with His own in the courtyard of Chandrashekhara's house5.

Verse 9

तत्र नारद इवाबभौ महा-
ञ्छ्रीपतेः प्रथमजो द्विजोत्तमः।
दण्डवद्भुवि निपत्य सुरर्षिः
प्राणमन्मुनिरजात्मजोऽजितम्॥९॥

tatra nārada ivābabhau mahā-
ñchrīpateḥ prathamajo dvijottamaḥ|
daṇḍavadbhuvi nipatya surarṣiḥ
prāṇamanmunirajātmajo'jitam||9||

tatra — there; naradah — Narada; iva — as; ababhau — appeared; mahan — the great; shripateh — of Shripati; prathama-jah — the elder brother; dvija-uttamah — the best of the twice-born; danda-vat — like a rod; bhuvi — on the ground; nipatya — falling; sura-rishih — the divine sage; pranamat — bowed down; munih — the sage; aja-atmajah — son of the Unborn (Brahma); ajitam — to the Unconquered.

9There the best of the twice-born, the great elder brother of Shripati, appeared as Narada6 — the divine sage, son of the Unborn, fell to the ground like a rod and bowed down to the Unconquered One.

Verse 10

मां प्रतीहि शनकैरिदमुक्त्वा
श्रीगदाधरमहीसुरमाह।
गोपिकेऽवदः सुरर्षिपदे त्वं
संप्रणम्य नतकन्धरचित्ता॥१०॥

māṁ pratīhi śanakairidamuktvā
śrīgadādharamahīsuramāha|
gopike'vadaḥ surarṣipade tvaṁ
saṁpraṇamya natakandharacittā||10||

mam — me; pratihi — recognize; shanakaih — softly; idam — this; uktva — having said; shri-gadadhara-mahisuram — to the brahmana Sri Gadadhara; aha — said; gopike — O gopi; avadah — you said; sura-rishi-pade — at the feet of the divine sage; tvam — you; sampranamya — bowing down; nata-kandhara-chitta — with neck and heart bowed.

10"Recognize me," he said softly to the brahmana Sri Gadadhara, and went on: "O gopi, you bowed down at the feet of the divine sage, bending your neck and your heart, and said:

Verse 11

तातमातृचरणं परिहृत्य
कृष्णपादकमलस्य सुसेवाम्।
कर्तुमीश इह तत्करुणाब्धेः
पादपद्मकरुणा मयि ते स्यात्॥११॥

tātamātṛcaraṇaṁ parihṛtya
kṛṣṇapādakamalasya susevām|
kartumīśa iha tatkaruṇābdheḥ
pādapadmakaruṇā mayi te syāt||11||

tata-matri-charanam — the feet of father and mother; parihritya — leaving; krishna-pada-kamalasya — to Krishna's lotus feet; su-sevam — devoted service; kartum — in order to render; isha — O master; iha — here; tat-karuna-abdheh — of Him, the ocean of mercy; pada-padma-karuna — the mercy of the lotus feet; mayi — on me; te — your; syat — may there be.

11'Master, I have left my father and mother to serve the lotus feet of Krishna here — so let the mercy of your lotus feet be upon me, that I may serve Him, the ocean of mercy.'

Verse 12

एवमाप्तवचसा स मुनिस्तां
संप्रहृष्टवदनः पुनराह।
अप्सरे सुरनदीपयसि त्वं
माघमासशतकैः सदा कुरु॥१२॥

evamāptavacasā sa munistāṁ
saṁprahṛṣṭavadanaḥ punarāha|
apsare suranadīpayasi tvaṁ
māghamāsaśatakaiḥ sadā kuru||12||

evam — thus; apta-vachasa — by sincere words; sah — that; munih — sage; tam — to her; samprahrishta-vadanah — his face beaming with joy; punah — in reply; aha — said; apsare — O apsara; sura-nadi-payasi — in the waters of the river of the gods; tvam — you; magha-masa-shatakaih — for hundreds of months of Magha; sada — constantly; kuru — perform.

12Then, hearing your sincere words, the sage, his face beaming with joy, answered you: 'Apsara, for hundreds of months of Magha, constantly perform in the waters of the river of the gods

Verse 13

स्नानमेकमनसा तदा भवेत्
कृष्णपादकमलस्य सुसेवा।
तत्कृतं मुनिवचो हि भवत्या
तेन गोकुल इहाभवज्जनिः॥१३॥

snānamekamanasā tadā bhavet
kṛṣṇapādakamalasya susevā|
tatkṛtaṁ munivaco hi bhavatyā
tena gokula ihābhavajjaniḥ||13||

snanam — bathing; eka-manasa — with a single-pointed mind; tada — then; bhavet — there will be; krishna-pada-kamalasya — to Krishna's lotus feet; su-seva — devoted service; tat — that; kritam — was done; muni-vachah — the sage's word; hi — indeed; bhavatya — by you; tena — through that; gokule — in Gokula; iha — here; abhavat — came about; janih — birth.

13your bath with a single-pointed mind — then you will attain the service of Krishna's lotus feet.' You carried out the sage's word, and because of it you were born here in Gokula7,

Verse 14

उत्तमामतितरां हरिभक्तिं
प्रेमनिर्भररसोर्मिभिरार्द्रा।
दुर्लभां त्रिजगतो मुनेरपि
यां प्रगायति मुदा शुकदेवः॥१४॥

uttamāmatitarāṁ haribhaktiṁ
premanirbhararasormibhirārdrā|
durlabhāṁ trijagato munerapi
yāṁ pragāyati mudā śukadevaḥ||14||

uttamam — the highest; atitaram — surpassing all; hari-bhaktim — devotion to Hari; prema-nirbhara-rasa-urmibhih — by waves of rasa full of love; ardra — moistened; durlabham — hard to attain; tri-jagatah — in the three worlds; muneh — for a sage; api — even; yam — which; pragayati — sings; muda — joyfully; shuka-devah — Shukadeva.

14and, moistened by the waves of a rasa full of love, you attained the highest devotion to Hari, surpassing all, which is hard to attain in the three worlds even for a sage — the devotion that Shukadeva joyfully sings.

Verse 15

तथा च —
वन्दे नन्दव्रजस्त्रीणां पादरेणुमभीक्ष्णशः।
यासां हरिकथोद्गीतं पुनाति भुवनत्रयम्॥१५॥

tathā ca —
vande nandavrajastrīṇāṁ pādareṇumabhīkṣṇaśaḥ|
yāsāṁ harikathodgītaṁ punāti bhuvanatrayam||15||

tatha cha — and so (it is said); vande — I revere; nanda-vraja-strinam — of the women of Nanda's Vraja; pada-renum — the dust of the feet; abhikshnashah — constantly; yasam — whose; hari-katha-udgitam — singing of the narrations of Hari; punati — purifies; bhuvana-trayam — the three worlds.

15As it is said: 'Again and again I revere the dust of the feet of the women of Nanda's Vraja, whose singing of Hari purifies the three worlds.'8

Verse 16

किं वदामि हरिभक्तिमहत्त्वं
सर्वपापगणवान्द्विजसूनुः।
दुःखपालिभिरजामिलनामा
पुत्रमात्रमनुचिन्त्य जगाम॥१६॥

kiṁ vadāmi haribhaktimahattvaṁ
sarvapāpagaṇavāndvijasūnuḥ|
duḥkhapālibhirajāmilanāmā
putramātramanucintya jagāma||16||

kim — what; vadami — shall I say; hari-bhakti-mahattvam — of the greatness of devotion to Hari; sarva-papa-ganavan — burdened with every sin; dvija-sunuh — a brahmana's son; duhkha-palibhih — (seized) by the guardians of torment; ajamila-nama — named Ajamila; putra-matram — only of his son; anuchintya — thinking; jagama — departed.

16What shall I say of the greatness of devotion to Hari? A brahmana's son named Ajamila, laden with every sin, seized by the guardians of torment, merely thought of his son — and went free9.

Verse 17

नाममात्रविभवेन भवाब्धेः
पारमेव परदुस्तरस्य च।
गच्छतु सगण एव कृपाब्धे-
र्धाम किं पुनरजस्य सुसेवा॥१७॥

nāmamātravibhavena bhavābdheḥ
pārameva paradustarasya ca|
gacchatu sagaṇa eva kṛpābdhe-
rdhāma kiṁ punarajasya susevā||17||

nama-matra-vibhavena — by the power of the mere name; bhava-abdheh — of the ocean of existence; param — to the far shore; eva — indeed; para-dustarasya — so very hard to cross; cha — and; gachchhatu — let one reach; sa-ganah — with companions; eva — even; kripa-abdheh — of the Ocean of mercy; dhama — the abode; kim punah — how much more; ajasya — to the Unborn; su-seva — devoted service.

17If by the power of the mere name one reaches the far shore of the ocean of existence, so very hard to cross, and even, with one's companions, the abode of the Ocean of mercy, how much more, then, by devoted service to the Unborn!"

Verse 18

एवमुक्तवति भूसुरवर्ये
प्रेमसागररसोर्मिभिरार्द्राः।
संबभूवुरति ते रसपूर्णा-
स्तूर्णमेव मुदिता द्विजवर्याः॥१८॥

evamuktavati bhūsuravarye
premasāgararasormibhirārdrāḥ|
saṁbabhūvurati te rasapūrṇā-
stūrṇameva muditā dvijavaryāḥ||18||

evam — thus; uktavati — when (he) had spoken; bhu-sura-varye — the best of brahmanas; prema-sagara-rasa-urmibhih — by waves of the rasa of the ocean of love; ardrah — moistened; sambabhuvuh — became; ati — exceedingly; te — those; rasa-purnah — full of rasa; turnam eva — at once; muditah — joyful; dvija-varyah — the best of the twice-born.

18When the best of brahmanas had spoken thus, the best of the twice-born were at once filled with joy and rasa, moistened by the waves of rasa from the ocean of love.

Verse 19

यदङ्घ्रिनखचन्द्रिकाकिरणमात्रमेतत्परं
सुरेन्द्रमुनिपुङ्गवैः सहचरैर्हि ब्रह्मादिभिः।
कृतं सकलनिर्मलं गोपगोपीनामामृतै-
स्तदप्सरःकथादिकं मनुजभावमेव स्फुटम्॥१९॥

yadaṅghrinakhacandrikākiraṇamātrametatparaṁ
surendramunipuṅgavaiḥ sahacarairhi brahmādibhiḥ|
kṛtaṁ sakalanirmalaṁ gopagopīnāmāmṛtai-
stadapsaraḥkathādikaṁ manujabhāvameva sphuṭam||19||

yat — whose; anghri-nakha-chandrika-kirana-matram — a mere ray of the moonlight of the toenails; etat — this; param — supreme; surendra-muni-pungavaih — by the lords of the gods and the best of sages; sahacharaih — as companions; hi — indeed; brahma-adibhih — by Brahma and the others; kritam — enacted; sakala-nirmalam — wholly pure; gopa-gopi-nama-amritaih — with the nectar of the names of the cowherd men and women; tat — that; apsarah-katha-adikam — the story of the apsara and the rest; manuja-bhavam — the human mood; eva — only; sphutam — clearly.

19A mere ray of the moonlight of His toenails — that is the supreme; together with His companions, the lords of the gods, the best of sages, Brahma and the others, He enacted a wholly pure play, full of the nectar of the names of the cowherd men and women; and the story of the apsara and the rest clearly shows only His play in the role of a man10.

Thus ends the fifteenth sarga, "Description of the Gopis' Mood — Bhakti-yoga" (Gopi-bhava-varnana — Bhakti-yoga), of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Varaha is the incarnation of Vishnu as a boar who raised the Earth from the waters; "He whose body is sacrifice" is His standing epithet.
  2. The mood of Balarama (see sarga 2.14) gives way to the mood of Krishna with His flute.
  3. Bhishmaka's daughter is Rukmini, Krishna's consort; here the name refers to the Lord's wife (Vishnupriya).
  4. Murari ("Enemy of Mura") is a name of Krishna; here it is the Lord Himself, not the author of the poem.
  5. The play at the house of Chandrashekhara Acharya, in which the Lord took a woman's role and His companions played other parts, is also described at length in other lives of the Lord.
  6. Shripati's elder brother is Srivasa.
  7. Narada (Srivasa) reminds Gadadhara, who is playing a gopi, of her former birth as an apsara. This is the plot of the play being staged (cf. v. 19: the story of the apsara is only play). Some gopis did attain Vraja through sadhana, but Krishna's eternal companions, and above all Radha, whom Gadadhara embodies (see 2.3, the note to v. 17), are not former apsaras but His eternal internal energy.
  8. Bhagavata Purana 10.47.63 — Uddhava's words about the gopis of Vraja.
  9. Bhagavata Purana, canto 6, chapters 1–2: dying, the sinful Ajamila called out to his son named Narayana; the messengers of Yama withdrew, and he was saved.
  10. The verse is obscure; the reading and interpretation are conjectural.
